findings.summary: The other registered form of the same tool still reports delivered/consumed on a bare resume: decision_deliver(target_kind="dd", target_id=...) routes to deliver_decision_dd, which calls DdOwnerSource.resume (gate resume only, owners.py:162) and returns delivered/consumed without publishing the verdict to the board and without reading back that the single transferred -- defect 1's exact S10 failure mode, still reachable through the @mcp.tool face and pinned green by tests/test_decision_mcp.py:543. It is pre-existing and outside the spec's named fix target (_deliver_dd), so it is not a regression, but the spec's general tightening ("delivered/consumed only when the single transferred per the verdict") does not hold on this path.

Defect 6 residual: status.json is still written (control_plane.py:1176) and still machine-read in two places -- harvest_ops._terminal_of consumes its `terminal` as a last-resort fallback, and DdControlPlane.list serves cached terminal rows. The list path now has invalidation logic (non-terminal rows are recomputed), which fits the spec's "derived view with invalidation" alternative, and the harvest read is authority-first (result.json wins); but the criterion's "no longer read as a consumable cache" is only enforced by a source pin over two files (wake.py, fleet_state.py), not repo-wide.

The spec requires the registered @mcp.tool path as the test entry for the criteria block, but the defect 4 refusal-vocabulary assertions call the deliver_decision core directly rather than through the tool. The wrapper is thin (build_decision_mcp_server passes straight to deliver_decision), and both blocker red targets do use the FastMCP client, so the coverage risk is small -- but the refusal message contract is not asserted through the registered face.

The mandated product-consistency check (git diff between 26dd0a4 and 261fcd1 excluding .dev-dispatch) could not be executed: this reviewer has file inspection only, no shell or Git. Inspection of the worktree tree shows the review-stage additions confined to the reserved .dev-dispatch/ namespace (reviews/rc-.../review.json and feedback/index.json), consistent with a metadata-only materialization; the deterministic seal must be the authority for the mechanical diff.

Identity metadata disagreement: the sealed implement handoff records work_head_commit f072faf394ee38c1c430e6f3ee507623d90d0354, while the dispatch context names 26dd0a4ded8810f958dc1721ae4b04ca3785f818 as both the product commit and the implementation_subject_commit. Consistent with the materializer stacking a metadata-only commit on f072faf to produce 26dd0a4, but the two records label "work_head_commit" differently.
